intro: University City, MO is the default answer to "where do WashU (Washington University in St. Louis) students live off campus," and for good reason: it borders campus on one side and the Delmar Loop on the other, and generations of students have lived in its brick apartments and old houses. Quick geography note for out-of-towners: this is University City, Missouri, the suburb next to WashU, not the Philadelphia neighborhood Google keeps showing you.
The listings below are in U City right now, with walk times to campus and reviews from students who lived in them. Student housing is thickest in the blocks north of the Delmar Loop.
directAnswer: University City, Missouri sits directly northwest of WashU and is one of the most popular neighborhoods for students living off campus, with easy walks to both campus and the Delmar Loop. Rents here generally run below Clayton and the Central West End, and every listing on this page shows its live price.

faqs.q: How much do University City, MO apartments cost?
faqs.a: Less than Clayton or the Central West End and a bit more than Skinker-DeBaliviere, going by Zillow's rent data. Student-oriented buildings near the Loop cost more than older flats a few blocks back. Real rents are on each listing above.

faqs.q: How far is University City, MO from WashU?
faqs.a: Walkable, for most of the student blocks. Much of the housing students rent sits within a 10 to 25 minute walk of the Danforth campus, and each listing above shows its own computed walk time so you don't have to guess from a map.

faqs.q: Why do so many WashU students pick U City?
faqs.a: Proximity and price, in that order. You can walk to class and stumble home from the Loop, and rents benchmark lower than Clayton or the Central West End. The housing stock is older, which cuts both ways: character and porches, but read the reviews to learn how each landlord handles maintenance.

faqs.q: Are rents in University City, MO rising?
faqs.a: Yes. Zillow's rent index for ZIP 63130 was up 4.7% year over year as of August 2026, ahead of the St. Louis metro at 3.9%. Source: Zillow Research.

benchmarkNote: Neighborhood comparisons on this page cite Zillow's Observed Rent Index (ZORI), ZIP-level data as of August 2026 for ZIP 63130. Rents on listings are each landlord's current asking rent. Proximity does not publish averages computed from its own listings.
